plan.title: DocMonk upgrade plan: ship 1.0, retrieval quality, agents and MCP, team use

context.summary: A read of main at 710200a (no build or test run) found local mode feature-complete and v1.0.0 blocked on human tasks rather than code. This plan complements plans/improvement-roadmap.json: it sequences the roadmap's open packages and adds work the roadmap does not cover, namely the MCP manifest size, MCP resources and prompts, streaming and a UI page for ask, HTTP route detection for more frameworks, connectors, server-mode git sources, built-in authentication for HTTP MCP, and a few dependency and packaging items.

baseline.scope: 13 tools, mostly outputSchema; roughly 25k tokens if a client loads it whole

baseline.metric: evidence cross-language recall@10, MiniLM vs multilingual-e5-small
false support rate / false abstention rate

baseline.scope: linux x86_64, macOS arm64 and x86_64, windows x86_64

baseline.metric: roadmap work packages blocked on a human
baseline.value: H3, R1 (and R2 behind it), Q1, decision D1

findings.summary: The MCP tool manifest is about 102 KB, most of it output schemas, which costs an agent roughly 25k tokens of context when loaded whole.
MCP resources, resource templates and prompts are advertised but always empty.
The cloud provider defaults are dated model names (gpt-4o-mini, claude-3-5-haiku-latest) and ask never streams.
HTTP route detection covers Python decorators and C# attributes only; Express, Fastify, Spring, Go routers and ASP.NET minimal APIs are not detected although their languages are parsed.
Sources are local folders and git repositories only, and git sources work in local mode only; there is no connector for Confluence, Slack or Jira.
The Admin UI has search and a provider test but no page to ask a question and read a cited answer.
There is no native Linux arm64 release archive; arm64 Linux is served by the container image only.
rusqlite is at 0.32, and three zip advisories are ignored in deny.toml until a 2027-01-31 review.
MCP over HTTP has no authentication of its own: it relies on a loopback bind or on an authenticating reverse proxy.
v1.0.0 is blocked on human tasks: no signing key is configured, the 100 held-out labels are unreviewed with empty floors, code-owner review is not enforced, and the server-mode decision is open.

evidence.note: H3 blocked, R1 not_started, Q1 blocked, D1 proposed

findings.summary: The default embedding model is far behind multilingual-e5-small on the held-out set, in English as well as across languages.

do_not_duplicate.summary: The improvement roadmap already specifies H3, R1 to R7, P1 to P5, P9, P11, A1 to A6 and Q1, Q2, Q6 with tasks and acceptance criteria. S1, S3, Q1 and T5 of this plan only sequence them.
Messaging topology (RabbitMQ, MassTransit, Kafka) is implemented; route work must reuse its graph-row and cross-source binding approach.
MCP visibility, query log, budgets and secret redaction exist; new MCP surfaces must go through them.
The Admin UI access model, CSRF and Host/Origin guards exist and cover the HTTP MCP router.
An embedding-model switch test and embedding ETA already exist.

rules: Branch from the latest main after every depends_on package is merged.
Keep security, retrieval-quality and refactor changes in separate PRs.
Tracking packages (S1, Q1, T5) use the branches of the roadmap packages they sequence.

protected_paths.reason: Held-out labels judge the code; a model must not approve its own labels.
Floors only move up, with human approval.
Finding statuses are claims about verification.
Must stay empty for the release gate.
Audits are never weakened to get CI green.

principles: Inspect current main before each work package; this plan was written from a read of 710200a without building or running the tests, so confirm each finding first and adapt where the code differs.
Measure before and after; never claim an improvement without a committed report.
Keep determinism: identical rankings, citations and verdicts on repeated runs over the same snapshot.
Every new read surface (resources, connectors, UI pages) goes through KnowledgeRead, secret redaction, MCP visibility and the query log.
Record design decisions as new ADRs in docs/adr/ with the next free number; the ADR numbers in this plan are placeholders.
Look up third-party API and model details at implementation time; do not take them from memory.
non_goals: No hosted or cloud service and no telemetry.
No connector that writes to the remote system.
No change to the ADR 0032 clean-slate policy.
No lowering of floors or loosening of audits to land a change.
No change of the default embedding model before roadmap decision D2 is recorded.

fetch_models.purpose: Download and verify the pinned embedding, reranker, OCR and E5 models.

test.purpose: Workspace tests with pinned models required, as in CI.

audits.run: cargo xtask clean-slate-audit && cargo xtask branding-audit
audits.purpose: Repository audits every new line must pass.

eval_default.purpose: Held-out eval with the default embedding model; attach the report.

eval_e5.purpose: Held-out eval with multilingual-e5-small; attach the report.

validate_plan.purpose: Validate this plan against its schema after every edit; then re-check x-integrity-rules by reading.

objectives.objective: Ship v1.0.0 with human-verified quality gates.
success_criteria: v1.0.0 is signed and installs on Linux, macOS, Windows and as a container.
Held-out floors on human-approved labels run nightly.

objectives.objective: Make the better embedder the default without breaking existing homes.
success_criteria: multilingual-e5-small is the default and installs with one command.
False support 0 and false abstention below 0.10 on approved labels.
A home indexed with another model never mixes vector spaces.

objectives.objective: Make DocMonk cheap and complete for agents.
success_criteria: Resources and prompts are available under the same visibility and redaction rules as tools.
Agent-flow ceilings are enforced in CI.

objectives.objective: Make DocMonk useful to a team sharing one index.
success_criteria: Server mode is GA with published measurements.
HTTP routes are detected for the main frameworks of all parsed web languages.
At least one connector (Confluence) indexes incrementally.
HTTP MCP can authenticate without a reverse proxy.
No ignore in deny.toml carries a past review date.
A native Linux arm64 archive ships with every release.

gate.criterion: Every held-out label is human-reviewed and floors are set.

work_packages.title: Clear the human release blockers from the roadmap
work_packages.purpose: Four items in plans/improvement-roadmap.json wait on a maintainer, not on code: the signing key (H3), the held-out label review (R1), code-owner review on main (Q1-03) and the server-mode decision (roadmap D1). Nothing else in this plan is trustworthy until the labels are human-reviewed.

tasks.title: Create the signing key
tasks.details: Generate a minisign keypair, keep the secret key offline, commit the public key to install.sh and install.ps1, and set vars.MINISIGN_PUBLIC_KEY plus the signing secrets in the repository (roadmap H3-01, H3-02).

tasks.title: Review the held-out labels
tasks.details: Review all 100 queries in fixtures/eval/queries.json, mark each approved or corrected, then set the floors in fixtures/eval/heldout-gates.json (roadmap R1-01, R1-02).

tasks.title: Require code-owner review
tasks.details: Turn on required code-owner review for main in the repository settings (roadmap Q1-03).

tasks.title: Decide server mode for 1.0
tasks.details: Record roadmap decision D1. Recommendation: preview, so the tag does not wait for the live 8k and 50k file measurements.

tasks.title: Update the roadmap file
tasks.details: Set the status fields and progress_log entries for H3, R1, Q1 and D1 in plans/improvement-roadmap.json.

acceptance.criterion: A release built by the workflow carries a valid SHA256SUMS.minisig and the installers refuse a tampered archive.
Every held-out query has a human review mark and heldout-gates.json has non-empty floors.
Roadmap decision D1 has status decided.

work_packages.rollback: Not applicable for the review and the decision. To rotate the key, commit a new public key and re-sign the latest release.
notes: This package only tracks roadmap items; the detailed tasks and acceptance criteria stay in plans/improvement-roadmap.json.

work_packages.title: Current default models for the cloud AI providers
work_packages.purpose: The OpenAI and Anthropic defaults in docmonk-ai are dated model names. A first-time user of docmonk ask with a cloud provider should get a model that is current and still served.

tasks.title: Pick the models
tasks.details: Read each provider's current model list and deprecation page at implementation time and propose one small, cheap default per provider. Do not take model names from memory. Decision D1 of this plan records the choice.

tasks.title: Change the constants
tasks.details: Update OPENAI_DEFAULT_MODEL and ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL in crates/docmonk-ai/src/http.rs and any registry entry that repeats them.

tasks.title: Refresh fixtures and docs
tasks.details: Regenerate the golden fixtures with DOCMONK_BLESS=1, check the diff contains only the model names, and update the ai.model rows in docs/reference.md.

acceptance.criterion: No retired or deprecated model name remains in crates/docmonk-ai or docs/reference.md.
The docmonk-ai golden tests pass with the new defaults.

work_packages.rollback: Revert the commit.

work_packages.title: Cut v1.0.0
work_packages.purpose: Finish the roadmap's release packages (R2 nightly held-out eval, R6 hygiene, R7 tag) once the human blockers are cleared.

tasks.title: Nightly held-out eval
tasks.details: Add the held-out eval job with failure reporting to the nightly workflow (roadmap R2).

tasks.title: Mark server mode as decided
tasks.details: Apply roadmap decision D1 to README.md, CHANGELOG.md and docs/reference.md.

tasks.title: Check the gates
tasks.details: Run every roadmap M0 and M1 gate, including the release gate audit, and list the results in the PR (roadmap R7-01).

tasks.title: Tag
tasks.details: A maintainer tags v1.0.0 from a green main (roadmap R7-02).

tasks.title: Verify installs
tasks.details: Install and run docmonk update on Linux, macOS and Windows and pull the container image; record the versions seen (roadmap R7-03).

acceptance.criterion: The release gate audit passes with an empty baseline.
v1.0.0 is published, signed, and installs on all three platforms and as a container.

work_packages.rollback: Delete the tag and the release, fix, and tag again; installed binaries roll back with docmonk update.

work_packages.title: Run the roadmap's retrieval packages
work_packages.purpose: The measured gap is the default embedder: evidence recall at 10 is 0.854 with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and 0.979 with multilingual-e5-small, and cross-language recall is 0.231 against 1.0. The roadmap already specifies the work (P1, P2, P3, P4, Q2 and decisions D2, D3); this package sequences it.

tasks.title: Models command
tasks.details: Roadmap P1: docmonk models list, install and remove with checksum verification, plus the optional full release asset.

tasks.title: Model-aware chunk budget
tasks.details: Roadmap P2: resolve documents.chunking.max_tokens auto per model and count with that model's tokenizer; re-run the held-out eval.

tasks.title: Record D2 and D3
tasks.details: Roadmap decisions D2 (default model) and D3 (bundled or on demand). Recommendation: multilingual-e5-small as default, installed on demand, MiniLM kept as a lite profile.

tasks.title: Abstention and ambiguity
tasks.details: Roadmap P4: bring false support (0.083) to 0 and false abstention (0.136) under 0.10 on approved labels.

tasks.title: Reranker language guard
tasks.details: Roadmap P3-01: never run the English cross-encoder on non-English queries. Keep the reranker off by default.

tasks.title: Grow the held-out set
tasks.details: Roadmap Q2: at least 300 approved queries with a sealed split.

acceptance.criterion: multilingual-e5-small installs with one command on every platform.
False support is 0 and false abstention is below 0.10 on approved labels, with no floor lowered.

deliverables: Roadmap P1 to P4 and Q2 merged
work_packages.rollback: Each roadmap package has its own rollback; the default model reverts with one config constant.
notes: Tracking package: branches and PRs are those of the roadmap packages, one each.

work_packages.title: Switching the embedding model on an existing home
work_packages.purpose: Changing the default embedder changes the vector space. A home indexed with MiniLM must not silently mix vectors, and the user needs one clear command and an estimate.

tasks.title: Audit current behaviour
tasks.details: Read embedding_model_switch.rs and the fingerprint code to establish what already happens when search.embedding_model changes; write the gaps down in the PR before changing anything.

tasks.title: Detect and report
tasks.details: status and doctor report a source whose stored vectors come from another model, with the command that fixes it and the embedding ETA that status already computes.

tasks.title: Keep serving meanwhile
tasks.details: Until re-embedding finishes, semantic search for that source is skipped with a reported state; lexical, symbol and graph results are unaffected.

tasks.title: Document the upgrade
tasks.details: A short section in README.md and the CHANGELOG entry for the release that flips the default.

acceptance.criterion: A home indexed with MiniLM, switched to E5, never returns a semantic hit computed across two models.
docmonk status names the affected sources and the fix.

work_packages.rollback: Revert the PR; stored vectors are untouched by the guard.

work_packages.title: A token budget for the MCP tool manifest
work_packages.purpose: crates/docmonk-mcp/src/mcp_tools.json is about 102 KB for 13 tools, most of it outputSchema. A client that loads tools/list whole spends roughly 25k tokens of agent context before the first call.

tasks.title: Measure
tasks.details: Add a test that serialises the tools/list result and reports its bytes and an approximate token count, per tool and in total. Commit the baseline numbers in the PR.

tasks.title: Collapse output schemas
tasks.details: Serve a minimal outputSchema by default (top-level keys and types only) and keep the full schemas behind a config key, pending decision D2 of this plan. structuredContent itself does not change.

tasks.title: Shorten descriptions
tasks.details: Rewrite tool and parameter descriptions to one or two sentences that say when to use the tool; move reference detail to docs/reference.md.

tasks.title: Gate it
tasks.details: The manifest test fails when tools/list exceeds the budget, so the manifest cannot grow back unnoticed.

acceptance.criterion: The default tools/list result is under 20 KB (about 5k tokens).
Every tool call still validates against the full schema in tests.

work_packages.rollback: Revert the PR; the previous manifest is one file.

work_packages.title: Compact output mode for retrieval tools
work_packages.purpose: Agents often need only the citation list to decide the next call. A compact mode lets them trade detail for context without changing ranking or verification.

tasks.title: Add the parameter
tasks.details: A detail parameter (compact or full, default full) on docmonk_explore, docmonk_search and docmonk_evidence.

tasks.title: Define compact
tasks.details: Compact returns each citation's source, path, location, evidence class and a one-line snippet, and omits expanded context. Verdicts and citation fingerprints stay.

tasks.title: Follow-up path
tasks.details: Confirm docmonk_read can fetch the full span for any compact citation, and say so in the tool description.

acceptance.criterion: Compact and full return the same citations in the same order for every golden MCP query.
Compact responses are at most a third of the full response size on the golden queries.

work_packages.rollback: Revert the PR; the default stays full.

work_packages.title: MCP resources and prompts
work_packages.purpose: resources/list, resources/templates/list and prompts/list return empty lists today. Resources let clients attach a document or symbol by URI; prompts give users the evidence-first workflow in one pick.

tasks.title: ADR
tasks.details: Write the ADR with the next free number: URI scheme for documents, chunks and symbols, pagination, and how mcp.hidden_sources and redaction apply.

tasks.title: Resource templates and reads
tasks.details: Implement resources/templates/list and resources/read over the KnowledgeRead port, pinned to the published build like every other read.

tasks.title: Prompts
tasks.details: Two prompts: answer with evidence (explore then evidence, cite or abstain) and impact review (impact on a symbol, then linked specs).

tasks.title: Same guards as tools
tasks.details: Hidden sources are not listed or readable, secrets stay redacted, and every read is written to the MCP query log.

acceptance.criterion: A hidden source cannot be listed or read as a resource.
No planted secret is readable through resources/read.
The initialize result advertises resources and prompts and both lists are non-empty.

work_packages.rollback: Revert the PR; the lists return empty again.

work_packages.title: Streaming answers for docmonk ask
work_packages.purpose: ask sends stream false and prints the answer when the provider finishes. Streaming makes local models usable interactively and is a precondition for a chat page.

tasks.title: Provider trait
tasks.details: Add a streaming call to the provider abstraction with a non-streaming fallback, so Codex and Copilot keep working unchanged.

tasks.title: HTTP providers
tasks.details: Implement server-sent-event streaming for the Ollama, OpenAI-compatible, OpenAI and Anthropic providers within the existing deadline handling.

tasks.title: CLI
tasks.details: docmonk ask prints tokens as they arrive on a terminal and stays buffered for --json and for pipes.

tasks.title: Citations
tasks.details: Citation verification still runs on the complete answer; the verdict is printed after the stream ends.

acceptance.criterion: The final text and verdict of a streamed answer equal the non-streamed ones against the mock provider.
--json output is byte-identical to before.

work_packages.rollback: Revert the PR; ask falls back to buffered answers.

work_packages.title: Ask page in the Admin UI
work_packages.purpose: The Admin UI can test a provider and run search but has no page to ask a question and read a cited answer. Roadmap P9 adds a search playground; this adds the ask counterpart.

tasks.title: Route and template
tasks.details: GET and POST /ask under the existing access model and CSRF protection, rendering the answer, its verdict and each citation as a link to the document or symbol page.

tasks.title: Streaming
tasks.details: Stream the answer over the same server-sent-event mechanism the indexing page uses.

tasks.title: No provider configured
tasks.details: Without a provider the page shows the evidence package only and links to the AI settings page.

acceptance.criterion: POST /ask without a CSRF token is refused.
The page renders an answer with citations against the mock provider.

work_packages.rollback: Revert the PR.

work_packages.title: Agent-flow evaluation
work_packages.purpose: Retrieval quality is measured; the cost of using DocMonk from an agent is not. Track manifest size, tool calls and response bytes per answered question so A1 and A2 are proven and regressions show.

tasks.title: Scripted flows
tasks.details: A deterministic scripted client answers a subset of the held-out queries through MCP alone, using fixed tool sequences per query category.

tasks.title: Report
tasks.details: Write a report with manifest bytes, calls per query, response bytes per query and whether the gold evidence was reached.

tasks.title: Gates
tasks.details: Add ceilings in fixtures/mcp/agent-flow-gates.json; a human approves the initial values.

acceptance.criterion: The report is reproducible byte for byte on repeated runs.
CI fails when a ceiling is exceeded.

work_packages.rollback: Revert the PR.
notes: Protect fixtures/mcp/agent-flow-gates.json as a never-raise ceiling once merged (add it to CODEOWNERS).

work_packages.title: HTTP routes for Express and Fastify
work_packages.purpose: Route detection covers Flask, FastAPI and ASP.NET attributes only. JavaScript and TypeScript is parsed for symbols, but its HTTP routes are not graph rows, so URL anchors, impact and cross-service questions miss them.

tasks.title: Rules
tasks.details: Detect app.get/post/put/patch/delete and router equivalents in Express, route registrations and shorthand methods in Fastify, and router mounting with a path prefix. Compose group or class prefixes with handler paths the way compose_routes does for C# controllers.

tasks.title: Graph rows
tasks.details: Emit the same route rows as the existing rules so exact URL occurrences, explore and impact pick them up with no retrieval change. Bump the graph derivation so graphs, not content, are recomputed.

tasks.title: Fixtures and tests
tasks.details: Add the fixture, extend the golden and endpoint tests, and include negative cases: a string that looks like a path but is not a route.

acceptance.criterion: Every route in the new fixture is found with its method and full path, and no negative case is reported.
A URL query for a fixture route returns its handler as an exact occurrence.
Held-out and repository eval reports are unchanged apart from added route hits.

work_packages.rollback: Revert the PR; the next index recomputes graphs with the previous derivation.

work_packages.title: Server mode from preview to GA

work_packages.title: Git remote sources in server mode
work_packages.purpose: Git sources are local mode only (ADR 0043). A team sharing one index needs a repository URL to be a source there too, with exactly one writer fetching it.

tasks.title: ADR
tasks.details: Decide where the checkout lives (the host holding the writer lease), how the indexed commit is stored in the server catalog, and what a second host does. Credentials still come only from git's own helpers.

tasks.title: Implement
tasks.details: Register, fetch and index a git source in server mode under the existing writer lease and fencing; status shows the indexed commit.

tasks.title: Failure cases
tasks.details: Unreachable remote or deleted branch marks the source offline and keeps the published index, as in local mode.

tasks.title: Live tests
tasks.details: Two-host test: only the lease holder fetches; the other reads the published build.

acceptance.criterion: A git source indexes and publishes on both engines.
Two hosts never fetch or publish the same source concurrently.

work_packages.rollback: Revert the PR; server mode refuses git sources again.

work_packages.title: Connector framework

requires.description: ADR and decision D3 before implementation.

work_packages.purpose: Sources are folders and git repositories. Team knowledge also lives in Confluence, Slack and Jira. Before any connector, fix the contract: how a remote system becomes documents with stable ids, incremental sync, deletions and credentials that never enter config.yaml or the index.

tasks.title: ADR
tasks.details: Write the ADR: a connector trait (list changed items since a cursor, fetch one item as bytes plus metadata, report deletions), source kind and config shape, credentials from environment variables only, rate limiting and backoff, offline behaviour, privacy (a connector is an outbound network call the user opts into per source).

tasks.title: Human review of the ADR
tasks.details: A maintainer approves the ADR and decision D3 of this plan before any code.

tasks.title: Crate and trait
tasks.details: Add crates/docmonk-connectors with the trait, a cursor store in the control database, and an in-memory fake connector used by tests.

tasks.title: Indexing integration
tasks.details: Connector items flow through the existing convert, redact, chunk and publish path; status shows last sync, cursor age and errors per source.

tasks.title: Layering
tasks.details: Add the crate to the workspace and to the layer table in docs/architecture.md; keep docmonk-core free of network dependencies.

acceptance.criterion: The fake connector indexes, updates and deletes items incrementally with no full rescan.
Planted secrets in connector content are redacted before storage.
cargo deny passes with any new dependency.

work_packages.rollback: Revert the PR; no stored data depends on the crate until a connector source is registered.

work_packages.title: Confluence connector

requires.description: A Confluence workspace and an API token with read-only scope for the live check.
The token, supplied through an environment variable.

work_packages.purpose: Index spaces and pages with their attachments from Confluence as cited documents through the connector framework, read-only, with the page or message URL as the citation target.

tasks.title: Read the API docs

work_packages.title: Token authentication for the HTTP MCP endpoint

requires.description: ADR and decision D4 before implementation.

work_packages.purpose: HTTP MCP is safe on loopback and, remotely, only behind an authenticating reverse proxy. A team that wants to share one DocMonk needs a built-in option that does not depend on proxy configuration.

tasks.title: ADR and decision
tasks.details: Write the ADR and record decision D4 of this plan: static bearer tokens now, OIDC later or never. A maintainer approves before code.

tasks.title: Tokens
tasks.details: Bearer tokens read from environment variables or a file outside config.yaml, compared in constant time, each with a name and an optional list of visible sources.

tasks.title: Transport rule
tasks.details: A non-loopback bind still requires TLS in front; with tokens configured, a request without a valid token is refused with 401 before any JSON-RPC handling.

tasks.title: Audit
tasks.details: The MCP query log records the token name, never the token.

acceptance.criterion: A remote request without a token, with a wrong token, or for a source outside the token's list is refused.
Loopback behaviour without tokens configured is unchanged.
No token value appears in logs, status or the query log.

work_packages.rollback: Revert the PR; remote access again requires the authenticating proxy.

decisions.question: Which default models for the OpenAI and Anthropic providers?
options: The provider's current small, cheap model, looked up at implementation time
No default: require ai.model to be set for cloud providers
decisions.recommendation: The provider's current small model, re-checked at every minor release.
decisions.rationale: A default keeps docmonk ask one config line away; requiring a model avoids ever shipping a retired name but adds a step.
decisions.decision: The provider's current small, cheap model, looked up at implementation time; the names are listed in the S2 PR for maintainer approval (decided by the maintainer on 2026-11-10).

decisions.question: Should tools/list serve minimal output schemas by default?
options: Minimal by default, full behind a config key
Full by default, minimal behind a config key
decisions.recommendation: Minimal by default, full behind a config key.
decisions.rationale: Most clients pay for the manifest on every session and few validate structured output against the schema; the full schema stays available for those that do.
decisions.decision: Minimal by default, full behind a config key (decided by the maintainer on 2026-11-10).

decisions.question: Which connector first, and are connectors in scope for a local-first product?
options: Confluence first, then Slack and Jira
No connectors: document export-to-folder workflows instead
decisions.recommendation: Confluence first, then Slack and Jira, each opt-in per source.
decisions.rationale: Confluence pages are long-lived documents and map cleanly onto the existing HTML path; chat and tickets are noisier. Connectors make outbound calls, which the privacy stance must state plainly.

decisions.question: How should HTTP MCP authenticate without a reverse proxy?
decisions.recommendation: Static bearer tokens now; revisit OIDC only if a team asks for per-user identity.
decisions.rationale: Tokens are small, testable and enough for a team-shared read-only endpoint; OIDC adds a large dependency and attack surface.

risks.risk: This plan rests on reading the code, not running it; a finding may be wrong in detail.

risks.risk: Trimming the manifest breaks a client that relies on full output schemas.
risks.mitigation: Decision D2 and a config key that restores full schemas; structuredContent is unchanged.

risks.risk: Route heuristics produce false routes and pollute exact URL matches.
risks.mitigation: Negative fixtures in every route package and unchanged eval reports as acceptance.

risks.risk: Connectors weaken the local-first and no-outbound-calls promise and add credential handling.
risks.mitigation: ADR and decision D3 before code, per-source opt-in, environment-only credentials, read-only scopes, recorded fixtures.

risks.risk: Built-in HTTP authentication is done badly and gives false confidence.
risks.mitigation: ADR and human review first, constant-time comparison, TLS still required for non-loopback binds, refusal tests.

risks.mitigation: Server mode ships as preview in 1.0; T5 and T6 are batched.

risks.mitigation: Byte-identical before and after eval reports are the acceptance criterion; stop instead of blessing.
